recipe.description: Morceaux de cuisses de poulet mijotés dans une sauce onctueuse de pâte d'arachide, tomates et citron, servi avec du riz blanc.

Laisse mijoter 5 minutes supplémentaires, en remuant, jusqu'à ce que la sauce devienne onctueuse et nappe le poulet.

Serre le mafé bien chaud, accompagné du riz blanc.

recipe.title: Garlic‑Ginger Chicken & Broccoli Stir‑Fry over Steamed Rice
recipe.description: Tender chicken thighs and crisp broccoli tossed in a fragrant garlic‑ginger soy sauce, served on fluffy rice.
instructions: Rinse the 200 g of rice, then place in a pot with 400 ml water. Bring to a boil over medium heat, cover and simmer 12 minutes until the water is absorbed; fluff and keep covered on low heat.
While the rice cooks, cut the chicken thighs into bite‑size pieces.
Trim the broccoli into florets.
Mince the garlic cloves and grate the ginger (about 1 tbsp). Slice the spring onions, separating white and green parts.
Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok over high heat. Add the chicken pieces and stir‑fry 4 minutes, until the surface is lightly browned.
Check the chicken’s internal temperature: it must reach 74 °C with clear juices and no pink.
Add the garlic, ginger, and the white parts of the spring onions; stir‑fry 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add the broccoli florets, splash 2 tbsp water, and stir‑fry 3 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Stir in 3 tbsp soy sauce, a pinch of salt and white pepper; toss 1 minute to coat everything.
Serve the stir‑fry over the steamed rice and garnish with the green parts of the spring onions.
tips: If the broccoli is large, blanch it 2 minutes in boiling water before adding to the wok to keep the colour vivid.
For extra heat, add a pinch of red pepper flakes with the garlic.

recipe.description: Crispy, golden pancake packed with spring onions and optional broccoli florets, perfect as a light dinner or snack.

recipes.title: Simple Chicken Fried Rice

recipe.title: Simple Chicken Fried Rice
recipe.description: Quick one‑pan fried rice with chicken, eggs, and spring onions, flavored with garlic, ginger and soy sauce.
instructions: Rinse the 300 g of rice, then place in a pot with 600 ml water. Bring to a boil over medium heat, cover and simmer 12 minutes until the water is absorbed; spread the cooked rice on a tray to cool quickly, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (or use day‑old rice).
Trim the chicken thighs and cut into small cubes (about 2 cm).
Mince the garlic and grate the ginger (approximately 1 tsp). Slice the spring onions, separating white and green parts.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large wok over high heat. Add the chicken cubes and stir‑fry 5 minutes, until the surface is golden and the interior reaches 74 °C (clear juices).
Push the chicken to one side of the wok; add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, then pour in the beaten 2 eggs. Scramble quickly, breaking them into small pieces, until just set.
Add the minced garlic, grated ginger, and white parts of the spring onions; stir‑fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the cooled rice, breaking up any clumps. Stir‑fry 3 minutes, letting the rice heat through and develop a light crust.
Stir in 2 tbsp soy sauce, a pinch of salt and white pepper; toss 1 minute to coat evenly.
Remove from heat, garnish with the green parts of the spring onions and serve immediately.
tips: Day‑old rice works best because it is drier and fries without becoming mushy.
For extra veggies, toss in a handful of frozen peas or diced carrots (not in pantry, so omit if strict).

recipe.title: Arroz frito con huevo, maíz y aguacate
recipe.description: Arroz blanco salteado al estilo latino con huevo revuelto, maíz dulce y trozos de aguacate, una comida rápida y completa para el almuerzo.
instructions: Enjuaga el arroz bajo agua fría hasta que el agua salga clara.

Bate los 2 huevos con una pizca de sal y pimienta. Empuja la mezcla de cebolla y maíz a un lado de la sartén, vierte los huevos batidos y revuelve rápidamente, cocinando hasta que queden suaves.
Incorpora el arroz cocido a la sartén; mezcla bien y saltea 4 minutos, hasta que todo esté caliente y ligeramente dorado.
Corta el aguacate en cubos y exprime el jugo de 1/2 lima sobre ellos para evitar que se oxiden.
Sirve el arroz frito en platos y coloca los cubos de aguacate encima como garnish.

recipe.title: Riz sauté façon wok avec poulet rôti et courgettes
recipe.description: Une poêlée rapide qui transforme le riz et le poulet déjà cuits en un plat complet, léger et savoureux, parfait pour le dîner.
instructions: Émince l'oignon en fines lamelles.
Râpe les courgettes à la grosse lame puis presse légèrement pour enlever l'excès d'eau.
Dans une grande poêle ou un wok, fais chauffer 1 c. à soupe d'huile à feu moyen.
Ajoute l'oignon et fais-le dorer 3 minutes, jusqu'à ce qu'il devienne translucide.
Incorpore les courgettes râpées, fais revenir 4 minutes, jusqu'à ce qu'elles soient tendres mais encore légèrement croquantes.
Ajoute le riz cuit (2 portions) et émiette le poulet rôti (1 portion) en morceaux moyens.
Fais sauter 5 minutes à feu moyen‑vif, en remuant régulièrement, jusqu'à ce que le mélange soit bien chaud et que le riz commence à dorer légèrement.
Bats les 2 œufs dans un bol, verse-les dans la poêle en formant un petit puits au centre, puis mélange rapidement pour obtenir une texture brouillée.

Assaisonne avec 1 pincée de sel et de poivre, goûte et ajuste si nécessaire.
Sers immédiatement, directement dans l'assiette.

Pour plus de croquant, ajoute une petite poignée de cacahuètes grillées juste avant de servir.

recipes.title: Mediterranean Stuffed Aubergine with Chickpea‑Tomato Ragù

recipe.title: Mediterranean Stuffed Aubergine with Chickpea‑Tomato Ragù
recipe.description: Tender aubergine halves filled with a hearty chickpea‑tomato ragù, brightened with lemon and finished with a drizzle of tahini.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Slice each aubergine in half lengthwise and scoop out a shallow cavity, leaving about 1 cm of flesh attached to the skin.
Brush the cut sides with 1 tbsp olive oil, season with a pinch of salt, and place on a baking sheet, flesh side up.
Roast for 20 minutes on medium heat, until the flesh is softened and the edges are lightly browned.
While the aubergine roasts, dice the 4 tomatoes and mince the 2 garlic cloves.
Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat; add the garlic and sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the diced tomatoes, cumin, paprika, and a pinch of salt; cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes break down.
Stir in the chickpeas (drained if canned) and the chopped spinach; cook 4 minutes, until the spinach wilts.
Add the lemon juice and adjust seasoning with pepper.
Remove the roasted aubergine halves from the oven; fill each cavity with the chickpea‑tomato ragù.
Return to the oven and bake an additional 5 minutes, just to heat the filling through.
Drizzle each stuffed aubergine with 1 tbsp tahini before serving.
tips: If the aubergine flesh is very watery, pat it dry with a paper towel before roasting.
For extra depth, add a splash of vegetable broth while cooking the ragù.

recipe.title: One‑Pot Quinoa with Spinach, Tomato & Lemon‑Tahini Sauce
recipe.description: A quick, comforting one‑pot dish where fluffy quinoa absorbs a bright lemon‑tahini sauce, studded with spinach and juicy tomatoes.
instructions: Rinse the quinoa under cold water until the water runs clear.
Dice the 3 tomatoes and mince the 2 garlic cloves.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat; add the garlic and sauté 1 minute.
Add the diced tomatoes, cumin, and a pinch of salt; cook 4 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes soften.
Stir in the quinoa and toast lightly for 2 minutes, allowing the grains to coat with oil.
Pour in the vegetable broth, increase to medium‑high heat, and bring to a gentle boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the quinoa is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
While the quinoa cooks, whisk together the tahini, lemon juice, 2 tbsp water, and a pinch of pepper to form a smooth sauce.
When the quinoa is done, fold in the spinach; cover for 1 minute until wilted.
Remove from heat, drizzle the lemon‑tahini sauce over the pot, and gently toss to combine.
Adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed, then serve warm.

recipe.description: A fragrant, slow‑simmered stew where chickpeas and cubed aubergine soak up a tangy tomato‑lemon broth, perfect for a light evening meal.

recipe.description: Pâtes rapides nappées d'une sauce tomate parfumée au basilic, agrémentées de mozzarella fondante. Un plat réconfortant, équilibré et prêt en moins de 30 minutes.
instructions: Fais bouillir 800 ml d'eau dans une grande casserole, ajoute 1 pincée de sel et plonge les 200 g de penne ; cuisson 11 minutes à feu moyen, jusqu'à ce qu'elles soient al dente.
Pendant ce temps, émince l'ail et fais-le dorer 1 minute à feu moyen dans 1 c. à soupe d'huile d'olive.
Ajoute les 250 g de sauce tomate basilic, porte à légère ébullition et laisse mijoter 8 minutes, jusqu'à ce que la sauce épaississe légèrement.
Égoutte les penne et incorpore-les à la sauce, mélange 1 minute pour bien enrober les pâtes.
Coupe la mozzarella en dés de 2 cm, ajoute-la aux pâtes chaudes et remue jusqu'à ce qu'elle fonde légèrement, créant des filaments.
Assaisonne avec sel, poivre et quelques feuilles de basilic frais déchirées.
Dresse les penne dans deux assiettes, parsème d'un filet d'huile d'olive si désiré et sers immédiatement.
tips: Pour une texture plus crémeuse, ajoute une cuillère à soupe d'eau de cuisson des pâtes avant la mozzarella.
Si tu aimes le piquant, ajoute une pincée de flocons de piment rouge en même temps que la sauce.

recipe.title: Plantain and Egg Breakfast Skillet
recipe.description: A quick, energizing skillet of ripe plantains, spiced tomatoes and onions topped with soft‑cooked eggs – a classic West African breakfast on the go.
instructions: Peel the plantains and slice them diagonally into 1/2‑inch thick pieces.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a non‑stick skillet over medium heat; add the plantain slices and fry 3 minutes per side, until golden and slightly caramelised. Transfer to a plate and set aside.
In the same skillet, add the remaining 1 tbsp oil and the finely chopped onion; sauté 2 minutes over medium heat until translucent.
Add the diced tomatoes and a pinch of salt; cook 4 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes break down into a chunky sauce.
Stir in the ground cayenne pepper and black pepper; taste and adjust seasoning.
Create two small wells in the sauce, crack an egg into each well, and cover the skillet.
Cook 4 minutes on low heat, until the egg whites are set and the yolks are still runny (internal temperature of the whites reaches 71 °C).
Return the fried plantain slices to the skillet, nestling them around the eggs; warm for 1 minute.
Serve hot, directly from the skillet.
tips: Use very ripe (yellow‑black) plantains for the sweetest flavor.
If you prefer fully set yolks, cook an additional 2 minutes uncovered.

recipe.title: Black‑Eyed Bean and Tomato Stew with Fried Plantain Chips
recipe.description: Hearty black‑eyed bean stew simmered with tomatoes and onion, served with crisp plantain chips – a satisfying mid‑morning or light lunch dish from West Africa.

Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a separate pan over medium‑high heat; fry the plantain rounds 2 minutes per side, until crisp and golden.
Transfer the fried plantain chips to paper towels to drain excess oil.
Taste the stew and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve the bean stew in bowls, topping each with a handful of plantain chips.

recipe.title: Tofu sauté au chou chinois et riz basmati
recipe.description: Un plat simple inspiré du wok chinois : tofu ferme doré, chou chinois croquant et riz basmati parfumé, le tout sauté rapidement avec sauce soja et gingembre.
instructions: Rince le riz basmati à l'eau froide, puis le mettre dans une casserole avec 400 ml d'eau. Porte à ébullition, couvre, baisse le feu à doux et laisse cuire 12 minutes, jusqu'à absorption complète. Retire du feu, laisse reposer 5 minutes, puis aère à la fourchette.
Pendant ce temps, coupe le tofu en cubes de 2 cm.
Émince finement le chou chinois en lanières d'environ 3 mm d'épaisseur.
Dans un wok ou une grande poêle, chauffe 1 c. à soupe d'huile à feu moyen‑vif. Ajoute les cubes de tofu et fais dorer 4 minutes, en les retournant jusqu'à ce qu'ils soient dorés sur toutes les faces.
Ajoute le gingembre râpé et le chou chinois. Sauté 3 minutes à feu moyen, jusqu'à ce que le chou commence à s’attendrir mais reste croquant.
Verse la sauce soja, mélange bien, puis assaisonne avec 1 pincée de sel et de poivre. Cuire encore 1 minute.
Répartis le riz cuit dans les assiettes, puis garnis avec le mélange tofu‑chou. Serre immédiatement.
tips: Utilise du tofu pressé au préalable pour éliminer l'excès d'eau et obtenir une meilleure coloration.
Ajoute un filet de jus de citron vert à la fin pour une touche de fraîcheur.

recipe.description: Un riz frit rapide, parfumé au citron vert, tofu croustillant et chou chinois, inspiré des marchés de rue thaïlandais, parfait pour un dîner léger.

recipe.title: Tajín de cordero picado sobre couscous renovado
recipe.description: Un tajín rápido de cordero picado cocinado con especias suaves, servido sobre el couscous sobrante, transformándolo en un plato reconfortante y ligero para la cena.
instructions: Pica la cebolla y el pimiento rojo en cubos pequeños.
Ralla la zanahoria.
Calienta 2 cda de aceite de oliva en una sartén grande a fuego medio.
Añade la cebolla y sofríe 5 minutos, hasta que esté translúcida.
Incorpora el pimiento y la zanahoria rallada, cocina 3 minutos más.
Agrega el cordero picado, salpimienta y cocina 8 minutos, removiendo, hasta que la carne pierda todo color rosado y alcance 71 °C en el centro (la carne ya no debe estar rosada).
Espolvorea 1 cdita de comino y 1/2 cdita de cúrcuma, mezcla y cocina 2 minutos para que suelten aroma.
Escurre y enjuaga los garbanzos de la lata, añádelos a la sartén y cocina 3 minutos, hasta que estén calientes.
Mientras tanto, coloca las sobras de couscous en una cacerola a fuego medio y caliéntalas, removiendo, hasta que estén humeantes en el centro (aprox. 3‑4 minutos).
Mezcla el couscous caliente con la mezcla de carne y garbanzos, ajusta de sal si es necesario.
Sirve inmediatamente, decorado con un puñado de cilantro fresco si lo tienes.
tips: Para que el couscous quede suelto, desmenúzalo con un tenedor antes de mezclarlo con la carne.
Si te gusta un toque picante, añade una pizca de harissa o pimentón dulce.

recipe.title: Harira ligera con cordero y garbanzos
recipe.description: Una versión rápida de la tradicional harira marroquí, usando cordero picado y los garbanzos enlatados, acompañada de couscous sobrante convertido en croutones tostados al final.
instructions: Pica finamente la cebolla, la zanahoria y el pimiento rojo.
Calienta 2 cda de aceite de oliva en una olla grande a fuego medio.
Añade la cebolla y sofríe 4 minutos, hasta que esté dorada.
Incorpora la zanahoria y el pimiento, cocina 4 minutos más.
Agrega el cordero picado, salpimienta y cocina 7 minutos, removiendo, hasta que la carne esté bien cocida y no presente rastros rosados (alcance 71 °C en el centro).
Espolvorea 1 cdita de comino y 1/2 cdita de jengibre, mezcla y cocina 1 minuto.
Vierte 600 ml de agua y el tomate triturado, lleva a ebullición.
Reduce el fuego a medio‑bajo y deja hervir suavemente 15 minutos, removiendo ocasionalmente.
Escurre y enjuaga los garbanzos, añádelos a la olla y cocina 5 minutos más, hasta que estén calientes.
Mientras la sopa hierve, corta la ración de couscous sobrante en cubos pequeños.
En una sartén sin aceite, tuesta los cubos de couscous a fuego medio durante 4 minutos, hasta que estén dorados y crujientes.
Pica el cilantro y agrégalo a la harira justo antes de servir.
Sirve la sopa en cuencos y espolvorea los croutones de couscous por encima.
tips: Si deseas una textura más espesa, disuelve una cucharada de harina en un poco de agua y añádela al final de la cocción.
Puedes ajustar la intensidad de las especias a tu gusto, añadiendo una pizca de pimentón dulce.

recipe.title: Bocaditos de couscous rellenos de cordero y verduras
recipe.description: Pequeñas bolas de couscous reutilizado, rellenadas con un guiso de cordero, zanahoria y pimiento, fritas ligeramente para obtener un exterior crujiente y un interior jugoso.
instructions: Pica finamente la cebolla, la zanahoria y el pimiento rojo.
Calienta 2 cda de aceite de oliva en una sartén a fuego medio.
Añade la cebolla y sofríe 4 minutos, hasta que esté transparente.
Incorpora la zanahoria y el pimiento, cocina 3 minutos más.
Agrega el cordero picado, salpimienta y cocina 8 minutos, removiendo, hasta que la carne esté bien hecha y alcance 71 °C en el centro (sin rastros rosados).
Espolvorea 1 cdita de comino y 1/2 cdita de cúrcuma, mezcla y cocina 1 minuto.
Escurre y enjuaga los garbanzos, añádelos a la mezcla y cocina 2 minutos para que se integren.
Retira la sartén del fuego y deja enfriar ligeramente la preparación de carne.
En un bol grande, desmenuza las 2 raciones de couscous sobrante. Añade 1 cda de aceite de oliva y una pizca de sal, mezcla hasta que quede húmedo pero manejable.
Con las manos humedecidas, forma bolas de couscous del tamaño de una nuez.
Haz un hueco en cada bola y rellénalo con una cucharadita de la mezcla de cordero y verduras.
Cierra bien la bola, asegurándote de que el relleno quede completamente cubierto.
Calienta 1 cda de aceite de oliva en una sartén a fuego medio.
Fríe los bocaditos en tandas, 3 minutos por lado, hasta que el exterior esté dorado y crujiente.
Escurre sobre papel absorbente y sirve caliente, acompañados de una salsa de yogur si lo deseas.
tips: Si el couscous está demasiado seco, humedécelo con una cucharada de agua antes de formar las bolas.
Para un toque extra de aroma, añade una pizca de ras el hanout al relleno de carne.

recipe.title: Pork Tenderloin with Dijon‑Mustard Cream Sauce and Sautéed Leeks
recipe.description: A light evening dish featuring tender pork medallions coated in a silky mustard‑cream sauce, served with sweet sautéed leeks.
instructions: Trim the pork tenderloin and cut it into four equal medallions (about 150 g each). Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the pork medallions and sear 3 minutes per side, until browned and the internal temperature reaches 63 °C (check with a thermometer). Remove and keep warm.
While the pork rests, thinly slice the leeks (white and light green parts only) and finely mince the shallots.
In the same skillet, add 1 tbsp butter and the shallots. Sauté over medium heat for 2 minutes, until translucent.
Add the sliced leeks, a pinch of salt, and cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they turn soft and lightly caramelised.
Reduce the heat to low. Stir in the Dijon mustard, then pour the cream, scraping the browned bits from the pan. Simmer 4 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon.
Return the pork medallions to the skillet, spoon the sauce over them, and warm for 1 minute.
Serve each pork medallion on a bed of the sautéed leeks, drizzled with the remaining mustard‑cream sauce.
tips: If you prefer a richer sauce, finish with a small knob of butter just before serving.
Use a splash of white wine after deglazing the pan for extra depth (optional, not in pantry).

recipe.title: Pork Tenderloin Roulade with Gruyère, Shallot‑Mustard Filling and Green‑Bean Almondine
recipe.description: Thinly sliced pork rolled around a creamy mustard‑shallot filling, baked gently, and served with crisp green beans tossed with toasted almonds.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C.

Place the pork tenderloin on a cutting board. Using a sharp knife, slice it horizontally into a thin sheet about 1 cm thick, keeping the pieces attached at one end so you can roll them (butterfly technique). Pound gently with a meat mallet to even thickness.
Finely dice the shallots. In a small bowl, mix the diced shallots, Dijon mustard, and half of the grated Gruyère. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Spread the filling evenly over the flattened pork, leaving a 1 cm border. Roll the pork tightly, seam side down, and secure with kitchen twine or toothpicks.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in an oven‑proof skillet over medium‑high heat. Sear the roulade on all sides, 2 minutes per side, until golden.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and bake 15 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the pork reaches 63 °C. Remove, let rest 5 minutes, then slice into 1 cm rounds.
While the pork bakes, trim the green beans and discard any tough ends.
In a separate pan, melt 1 tbsp butter over medium heat. Add the green beans, a pinch of salt, and sauté 6 minutes, stirring, until they are bright green and just tender.
Add the sliced almonds and continue to toss for 2 minutes, until the almonds are lightly toasted.
Plate three pork roulade slices per person, sprinkle with the remaining Gruyère, and serve alongside the almondine green beans.
tips: If you lack kitchen twine, secure the roll with two toothpicks and remove before serving.
For extra aroma, add a splash of dry white wine to the pan after searing the roulade (optional).

recipes.title: Provencal Pork Tenderloin with Mustard‑Herb Crust and Leek‑Shallot Velouté

recipe.title: Provencal Pork Tenderloin with Mustard‑Herb Crust and Leek‑Shallot Velouté
recipe.description: A quick pan‑roasted pork tenderloin coated with a Dijon‑herb crust, accompanied by a smooth velouté made from leeks and shallots, finished with a hint of cream.
instructions: Preheat a heavy skillet (preferably cast‑iron) over medium‑high heat.
Pat the pork tenderloin dry. Rub the entire surface with Dijon mustard, then sprinkle evenly with Herbes de Provence, salt, and pepper.
Add 1 tbsp olive oil to the hot skillet. Place the pork whole in the pan and sear 4 minutes per side, until a deep golden crust forms.

Reduce heat to medium, add 1 tbsp butter, and continue roasting for 12 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 63 °C. Transfer the pork to a cutting board, cover with foil, and let rest 5 minutes.
While the pork rests, slice the leeks (white part only) and mince the shallots.
In the same skillet, add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil if needed. Sauté the shallots over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the leeks, a pinch of salt, and cook 6 minutes, stirring, until they are very soft.
Pour in 150 ml cream, scraping up any browned bits. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 4 minutes, stirring, until the mixture thickens slightly.
Blend the leek‑shallot mixture with an immersion blender for 30 seconds to achieve a smooth velouté; no need to strain.
Slice the rested pork into 1‑cm medallions. Plate the velouté, arrange pork slices on top, and drizzle with any remaining pan juices.
tips: For a smoother velouté, pass the sauce through a fine sieve before serving.
If you prefer a lighter sauce, replace half of the cream with low‑fat milk (not in pantry).
